name: DATE
description: DATE builds a date serial number from separate year, month, and day components, and automatically rolls over out-of-range values such as month 13 into the next year or day 32 into the following month.
tldr: Assembles a date from year, month, and day values.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year component. In Excel, values 0-1899 are added to 1900 (0 becomes 1900, 119 becomes 2019); values 1900-9999 are used as-is.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: The month component, 1-12. Values outside that range roll over into adjacent years (13 = January of the next year, 0 = December of the previous year).

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: The day component, 1-31. Values beyond the length of the month roll into the next month (day 32 of January becomes February 1).

basicExample.description: Combine separate cells into a real date
basicExample.explanation: Serial 45305 corresponds to 2024-01-15. Apply a date number format to display it as a calendar date.

advancedExamples.title: Month overflow rolls into next year
advancedExamples.description: DATE carries the overflow into the following year
advancedExamples.explanation: Month 13 is treated as January of the next year, so the result is 2025-01-01 (serial 45657).

advancedExamples.title: Day overflow rolls into next month
advancedExamples.description: Day 32 of a 31-day month spills into the next month
advancedExamples.explanation: January has 31 days, so day 32 becomes 2024-02-01 (serial 45322).

howItWorks: DATE validates the three integer inputs and converts them into an Excel date serial, the count of days since 1900-01-01 (serial 1). When any component exceeds its normal range, Excel carries the overflow into the next higher unit, so month and day values roll forward automatically.

howToSteps.name: Enter the year
howToSteps.text: Provide the four-digit year (or a value Excel will offset into the 1900-9999 range).

howToSteps.name: Enter the month and day
howToSteps.text: Provide month and day integers; out-of-range values roll over.

howToSteps.name: Format as date
howToSteps.text: Apply a date number format so the serial displays as a calendar date.

limitations: Excel only supports dates from 1900-01-01 onward; earlier dates return #VALUE!.
Two-digit or small year values are offset by 1900, which can be confusing (always use 4-digit years).
The result is a serial number and must be date-formatted to be readable.

commonErrors.cause: A non-numeric or out-of-supported-range argument (e.g. a year before 1900).
commonErrors.fix: Use a numeric year between 1900 and 9999.

commonErrors.cause: Supplying 2-digit years like 24, which Excel reads as 1924.
commonErrors.fix: Always use four-digit years such as 2024.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DATE works the same way in Google Sheets, but years 0-99 are mapped to 1900-1999 (e.g. 24 becomes 2024), unlike Excel which offsets by 1900.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Prefer four-digit years to avoid the year-mapping difference.

faq.question: Why does my DATE result show a number like 45305?
faq.answer: Excel stores dates as serial numbers; format the cell as a date to see 2024-01-15.

faq.question: What happens if I use month 13?
faq.answer: It overflows into the next year: DATE(2024,13,1) returns 2025-01-01.

faq.question: Does DATE work with cell references?
faq.answer: Yes, e.g. =DATE(A1,B1,C1) builds a date from three cells.
